logline: Money Heist's most theatrical villain - now the lead - assembles a crew of eccentric specialists to steal across Europe's grandest cities, one baroque heist per season.

bollymeter.basis: 70% on Rotten Tomatoes; critics found the Berlin spinoff enjoyable on its own terms but unable to recreate the momentum of the parent show - Pedro Alonso's performance remained compelling, but the ensemble felt thinner.

pull_quotes.text: Berlin coasts on Pedro Alonso's considerable charisma without quite finding the narrative engine that powered Money Heist.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 - subtitled 'The Jewels of Paris' - was received as a watchable but not essential spinoff. Álex Pina extracted Berlin from the Money Heist timeline and placed him in a pre-Mint caper in Paris with an ensemble that took most of the eight episodes to cohere. Pedro Alonso's Berlin remains one of Spanish television's most theatrical creations - all operatic ego and genuine menace - and the Paris setting was gorgeous. Critics at 70% noted that the show hadn't yet found the structural tension that made Money Heist compulsive. The flashback-within-flashback architecture confused more than it revealed.

bollymeter.basis: Season 2 (The Lady with an Ermine) improved on Season 1 critical reception; the Seville setting and a Professor cameo were noted positively, though the show remained a capable entertainment rather than a must-watch.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 - subtitled 'The Lady with an Ermine' - sent Berlin and his crew to sun-drenched Seville for a Da Vinci heist. Critics who'd found Season 1 functional found this an improvement: the ensemble had chemistry now, the visual storytelling was more confident, and a cameo from The Professor rewarded Money Heist loyalists. Still operating below the parent show's dramatic floor, but a spinoff that had found its own reason to exist - Berlin as a European heist anthology with a fixed eccentric center.
seasons.season_over_season: A clear improvement on Season 1 - the ensemble has settled, the setting is more vivid, and the show has found its own register distinct from Money Heist.
